Apple's major September launch event is just around the corner, at which three brand-new iPhone models will be unveiled: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the iPhone Ultra. Here's a preview of all the highlights.

iPhone 18 Pro 及 Pro Max

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will follow in the footsteps of Apple's hugely popular 17 Pro series.

Rumoured new features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, with further improvements in both performance and efficiency
  • Major camera system upgrade, with the main camera introducing a variable aperture design
  • Dynamic Island reduced in size by 35%, for a more modern look
  • New colour options, led by a striking burgundy
  • Best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing significant improvement
  • Comprehensive redesign of the Camera Control button
  • Adoption of Apple's in-house C2 modem chip
  • New satellite connectivity features, including 5G satellite connection

The iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to see a higher starting price. Outside estimates put the starting price at up to US$1,399, though the writer suspects the actual price will be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is reportedly set to become Apple's first foldable iPhone, with pricing expected to be above US$2,000, creating an entirely new premium market tier.

The foldable design will make the iPhone Ultra Apple's most groundbreaking model to date. The device adopts a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of approximately 5.4 inches and an inner display of approximately 7.8 inches, offering an experience similar to an iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to match those of the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame with a clean, minimalist look.

The iPhone Ultra will come equipped with two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) and two front cameras, corresponding to the inner and outer displays respectively. The unlocking method will switch from Face ID to Touch ID.

Software will be the biggest highlight of this device — iOS 27 will support side-by-side multitasking and automatically adjust the layout for landscape orientation, perfectly complementing the new form factor.

Overall performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also featuring the A20 Pro chip, a vapour chamber cooling system, and the C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, Apple should be launching the entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air simultaneously in September.

However, Apple is reportedly making significant changes to its autumn product lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this arrangement is purely a strategic decision or driven by current memory supply constraints. Either way, with no more affordable models in the mix, this autumn's new iPhone lineup will focus solely on the premium market.

Are readers planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model has caught your eye? Feel free to share in the comments section.
